items.stem: The weighted average cost of capital (WACC) is most appropriate as a discount rate when:

options.text: The project has the same business and financial risk as the company's existing operations
options.rationale: Correct: WACC is valid when risk profile is unchanged.

options.text: The project changes the company's gearing significantly
options.rationale: A material gearing change invalidates the existing WACC.

options.text: The project is in a completely different industry
options.rationale: Different business risk requires a project-specific rate.

options.text: The company is about to be liquidated
options.rationale: Liquidation is not the basis for using WACC.

items.explanation: Correct: WACC is valid when risk profile is unchanged.

items.stem: In a management buy-out, the key feature is that:

options.text: The existing management team acquires the business it runs
options.rationale: Correct: an MBO is an acquisition by the incumbent management team.

options.text: An external competitor acquires the business
options.rationale: That is a trade sale, not an MBO.

options.text: The company lists its shares for the first time
The company repays all its debt early
options.rationale: Debt repayment is not the defining feature of an MBO.

items.explanation: Correct: an MBO is an acquisition by the incumbent management team.
